headlines.text: It was 2022 when a new chapter began as Jon Moxley vs. Hiroshi Tanahashi fought for the brand-new AEW Interim World Title, appearing on Forbidden Door, rated 8.08 ? a fantastic contest. This first-ever singles meeting closed the show with Moxley putting Tanahashi through the timekeeper's table before locking in the Death Rider to become interim AEW World Champion.

It was 2021 when Kenny Omega vs. Jungle Boy clashed for the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.43 ? a hard-hitting, high-quality battle. A coming-of-age moment for the young star ? Jungle Boy earned his shot by eliminating Christian Cage from a Casino Battle Royale, and gave the champion a real scare, nearly forcing him to submit before outside interference saved the title reign.
Looking back to 2024, when it was Hiromu Takahashi's first night in AEW, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.15.

secondaries.text: On a Sunday in 2022, back when the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Title was crowned as PAC vs. Clark Connors vs. Malakai Black vs. Miro went to war, appearing on Forbidden Door, rated 7.74 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle. Connors, a late replacement for the injured Tomohiro Ishii, won over the Chicago crowd by spearing Miro through a table, but it was PAC who submitted him to become the first-ever All-Atlantic Champion.

Back on this day in 2022, Will Ospreay vs. Orange Cassidy put the IWGP United States Title on the line, appearing on Forbidden Door, rated 9.04 ? a match that lived up to every bit of hype. For Will Ospreay, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. Cassidy's laid-back style threw Ospreay off from the opening bell, and after a string of near-falls this one stole the show ? capped by a surprise Katsuyori Shibata debut chasing off the post-match beatdown.

Turning the clock back to 2022: Jay White vs. Adam Page vs. Adam Cole vs. Kazuchika Okada etched their names into history in the first-ever IWGP World Heavyweight Title match, appearing on Forbidden Door, rated 7.45 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle. White and Cole briefly worked together as Bullet Club allies before White turned on his own partner, sneaking in a Blade Runner to steal the pin on Cole and retain the title.
